hero.lead: A nation of 58.9 million with a €194.4 billion recovery and resilience plan, where public debt is 137.1% of GDP.

capital.heading: A recovery plan to reach every household.

record.text: Value of Italy’s recovery and resilience plan, €71.8 billion in EU grants and €122.6 billion in loans; the disbursement of the ninth instalment, €12.8 billion, was authorised on 22 May 2026
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: CDP social bond, February 2034
register.detail: Cassa Depositi e Prestiti · placed 9 February 2026 · eight years, due February 2034 · coupon 3.375% · demand above €4.6bn from more than 110 investors · international investors more than 85% of the allocation
register.note: The eighth CDP social bond, bringing its ESG issues since 2017 to twelve, worth €8bn in all
register.text: A social bond of Cassa Depositi e Prestiti, issued under its Green, Social and Sustainability Bond Framework for its eligible social categories. Its proceeds finance Italian small and medium-sized enterprises, with particular weight on those in economically disadvantaged areas of the country; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants €71.8bn and loans €122.6bn · first approved by the Council 13 July 2021 · ninth instalment of €12.8bn authorised 22 May 2026 · plan updated August 2026
register.note: 150 investment streams and 66 reforms; 39% of the plan supports climate objectives and 25.6% the digital transition
register.text: EU grants and loans under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Italy, paid in instalments against milestones and targets. The plan includes €15.7 billion for the healthcare system, with hospitals, home care and telemedicine, and €26.9 billion for education and active labour market policies, with childcare facilities and vocational training; it serves the health, education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Puglia Region sustainable development
register.detail: European Investment Bank · first tranche of €50M signed, announced 3 August 2026 · structural programme loan for the Region’s 2021–2027 ERDF Regional Programme · investment programme of about €2.34bn
register.note: A €150M package, of which the first €50M tranche is signed
register.text: An EIB loan to the Region of Puglia for selected investments of its regional programme financed by the European Regional Development Fund, in healthcare, education, water, wastewater, waste, energy, transport and natural resources. Expected results include new or redeveloped water, social, healthcare and education infrastructure; it serves the water, health and education standards.

register.name: Naples urban regeneration framework loan
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed, announced 9 June 2026 · framework loan to the City of Naples · planned investments of about €95.6M
register.note: Includes new affordable rental homes in the districts of Pianura and Chiaiano
register.text: An EIB framework loan to the City of Naples for new affordable rental homes in Pianura and Chiaiano, the construction and upgrading of public buildings including schools, social facilities and sports infrastructure, and green spaces, renewable energy and sustainable mobility. It serves the shelter and education standards.

register.name: Campi Flegrei reconstruction and seismic safety, Naples
register.detail: European Investment Bank · approved, release of 5 November 2025 · framework loan to the Italian Republic, signed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance in two programmes · project shown signed 17 December 2025 · works expected to be completed by 2032
register.note: Up to €1.4bn: up to €550M for private homes and up to €850M for public buildings
register.text: EIB financing of up to €1.4 billion to the Italian Republic for the reconstruction and seismic risk reduction of private residential buildings, and of public buildings and infrastructure, in the Campi Flegrei area of Naples. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Post-earthquake reconstruction in Central Italy (CDP)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 15 April 2025 in Rome · borrower Cassa Depositi e Prestiti, for its Plafond Sisma Centro Italia · third CEB–CDP operation, after 2018 and 2023
register.note: CEB resources for this reconstruction now exceed €1bn
register.text: A CEB loan to Cassa Depositi e Prestiti, channelled through participating banks to households and businesses as eligible reconstruction works progress, to rebuild private buildings and production facilities damaged by the earthquakes of 2016 and 2017. It serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: ACEA water infrastructure in Lazio
register.detail: European Investment Bank · €450M package approved · first tranche of €200M signed in Rome, announced 27 July 2026 · 2027 to 2030 investment plan
register.note: The 17th EIB–ACEA agreement since 1999, about €2.6bn in all
register.text: EIB finance for ACEA, the water operator, for its 2027 to 2030 investment plan for water supply, treatment, distribution and wastewater in its service areas in Lazio: upgraded networks, fewer water losses, digital systems, stronger interconnections and water reuse. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: AIMAG integrated water services, Province of Modena
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 9 July 2026 · announced 13 July 2026 · backed by InvestEU · green loan for the 2025–2029 water investment programme
register.note: More than 200 upgrades to water, sewerage and wastewater treatment infrastructure
register.text: An EIB loan to AIMAG, a multi-service company based in Mirandola, for its integrated water services in the Province of Modena: water supply and sewerage networks, new pipelines, fewer water losses and upgraded wastewater treatment plants, benefiting around 200,000 people. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Affordable and student housing framework loan (Intesa Sanpaolo)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240851 · approved 10 April 2026 · signed 8 June 2026 · total cost €600M
register.note: Lending by Intesa Sanpaolo for affordable and student rental housing
register.text: An EIB framework loan to Intesa Sanpaolo to support its lending for affordable housing, including student accommodation, and the energy upgrade of the related buildings. It serves the shelter and energy standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 11.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Last Minute Market
items.text: A social enterprise and accredited spin-off of the University of Bologna that has fought waste since 1998 by recovering surplus food and goods for charities; with Chef Express and Hera it recovered more than 14,000 food portions from catering points by the end of 2025, a scheme now covering 12 sites and as many charities from Friuli Venezia Giulia to Sicily.

items.name: DAR=CASA
items.text: A Milan housing cooperative that builds and manages affordable rented homes, such as the 48 apartments of via Carbonia 3 for young people and for families in housing emergency; in January 2026 it was letting studios there at €445 a month to students and workers aged 20 to 35 with incomes of up to €1,500 a month.

items.name: ènostra
items.text: A cooperative that produces and sells renewable electricity to its members and works with renewable energy communities, with 18,732 members and 19,068 active supply points at the end of 2025 and sales of €19.4 million that year.

items.name: Piazza dei Mestieri
items.text: A trades school founded in Turin in 2004 where 600 young people from the age of 14, many of whom had left school, study and work in cooking, baking, graphic design, IT and other trades, with a restaurant open to the public and a craft brewery; it has further sites in Milan and Catania.

items.name: Santagostino
items.text: A network of specialist clinics founded in 2009 that offers high-quality specialist medicine at affordable prices, including in areas the national health service does not cover, such as dentistry, psychotherapy and speech therapy; it has opened more than 50 centres, mainly in Lombardy, Emilia-Romagna, Liguria and Lazio.

items.name: PizzAut
items.text: A foundation whose pizzerias in Cassina de’ Pecchi and Monza, near Milan, are run with young autistic people, 41 of them hired on permanent contracts by September 2026; it has also bought five apartments for their independent living.

items.name: Giotto social cooperative
items.text: A social cooperative founded in Padua in 1986 that has given work to more than 1,500 inmates of the Due Palazzi prison, where it runs a call centre booking medical visits for the local health authority and assembly work for local firms, employing about 70 people in all.
